# Lakeguard
Source: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/lakeguard
Fetched: 2026-06-16
Last updated on page: Nov 5, 2025

## What is Lakeguard?
"Lakeguard is a set of technologies on Databricks that enforce code isolation and data filtering so multiple users can share the same compute resource securely and cost-effectively."

Applies to: standard classic compute, serverless compute, SQL warehouses.

## Classic Spark architecture (the problem)
"User applications share a JVM with privileged access to the underlying machine." — cross-user data leakage risk.

## Lakeguard architecture (the solution)
"Lakeguard isolates all user code using secure containers. This allows multiple workloads to run on the same compute resource while maintaining strict isolation between users."
Maintains strict boundaries between users, the Spark driver, and executors.

## Spark client isolation

### Spark Connect
"Lakeguard uses Spark Connect to decouple client applications from the driver. Client applications and drivers no longer share the same JVM or classpath."
"Spark Connect defers analysis and name resolution to execution time, which may change the behavior of your code."

### Container sandboxing
"Each client application runs in its own isolated container environment."
Prevents unauthorized data access between users.

## UDF isolation
- Sandboxes execution environments on Spark executors
- "Isolating egress network traffic from UDFs to prevent unauthorized external access"
- Replicates the client environment into the UDF sandbox

Scope:
- UDFs on standard compute: isolated
- Python UDFs on serverless compute and SQL warehouses: isolated
- (Implication: Scala/Java UDFs on serverless/SQL warehouses may lack equivalent isolation)

## Data filtering
Lakeguard prevents users from "accessing data resulting from over-fetching when queries include row- or column-level filters." Prevents cross-user data leakage through row/column security policies.
